extracted.intended_audience: journalism and media researchers and news media practitioners (editors, social‑sharing analysts)
extracted.subtask_short: predicting news sharing on social media
extracted.subtask_description: Identify article characteristics that predict whether news stories will be widely shared on social media; adapt traditional newsworthiness criteria to digital-era drivers like identity signaling and emotion. Useful for researchers modeling sharing and for editors optimizing content for social distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Local stories share well within a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that are geographically close to an audience are more likely to be shared by members of that community; useful when tailoring content to local social networks or audience segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories matching audience identity share more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content aligns with the cultural background, values, or group identity of readers it increases propensity to share as a form of identity expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreement or controversy triggers reactions that increase sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict-oriented stories provoke discussion and emotional responses that spur sharing; framing that highlights disagreement can increase virality but may have editorial trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative news tends to be shared more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative valence drives engagement and sharing in social media contexts; editors should note this bias when predicting spread or deciding framing strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of elite actors drives engagement and sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories involving elite individuals or institutions (politicians, celebrities, major organizations) attract attention and are more likely to be redistributed across networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events or developments with substantial consequences or scope increase perceived importance and therefore sharing likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotion‑evoking content
rubrics_metrics.description: High‑arousal emotions in content drive sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that elicits strong emotions (anger, awe, amusement) tends to be reshared more; consider emotional valence and arousal when assessing shareworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity‑signaling
rubrics_metrics.description: People share to express who they are; articles that enable identity signaling are more shareable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that allow sharers to communicate values, beliefs, or group membership increase share probability — e.g., articles that reflect ideological stance or social identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How‑to, tips, or information that helps readers perform tasks is more likely to be passed on because it provides tangible value to recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise / Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Unexpected or novel information increases sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surprising facts or new angles attract attention and prompt sharing as people pass along novel information to their networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to existing online conversations
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories tied to ongoing online conversations are more likely to be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an article links into hashtags, memes, or trending discussions, it benefits from network momentum and increased redistributability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length (negative predictor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer pieces are less likely to be reshared on social platforms — brevity facilitates quick consumption and easier redistribution; consider summarization or teasers for social posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity (negative predictor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex stories that are hard to summarize are shared less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High conceptual or contextual complexity reduces shareability because potential sharers face higher effort to explain or justify the content to their networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness versus Shareworthiness (conceptual implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness (editorial/institutional criteria) is not equivalent to shareworthiness (what drives social sharing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story deemed important by journalistic standards may flop on social media, and vice versa; practitioners should evaluate both traditional news values and digital‑era sharing drivers when predicting or optimizing social distribution.
